item.title: Yari never called Nigerian youths lazy – Group insists
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA — The Senator Yari National Unity Project for Tinubu 2027 has dismissed reports that Senator Abdul’aziz Abubakar Yari described Nigerian youths as lazy, accusing sections of the media of misrepresenting his remarks at the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Uyo, Akwa Ibom State. The group said Yari, Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, was speaking about hunger, food availability and the dignity of hard work, rather than disparaging young Nigerians. In a statement issued by its National Coordinator, Dr Sani Abdullahi Shinkafi, the group challenged those circulating the allegation to watch the full footage of Yari’s address, insisting that the senator had acknowledged the economic hardship facing Nigerians before making his remarks on productivity. “He opened his remark by stating plainly: ‘We have hunger.’ At no point in that remark did the Senator mention, single out or describe Nigerian youths. To turn a statement on the dignity of work, made by a man who had just acknowledged that hunger exists, into the headline ‘Yari calls youths lazy’ is not reporting; it is spin,” the statement said. To support its position, the group cited Yari’s interventions in education, military recruitment, agriculture and public-sector employment, arguing that his record demonstrated his commitment to the welfare and empowerment of young Nigerians. It also claimed that Yari facilitated the enlistment of 158 young people from Zamfara West into two Nigerian Army recruitment intakes and supported farmers with agricultural inputs and equipment. “A leader who sends thousands of young people to university and into national service does not hold Nigerian youths in contempt; he invests in them,” the statement added. The group reaffirmed its confidence in Yari and directed its officers nationwide to intensify grassroots mobilisation for President Bola Tinubu and Vice President Kashim Shettima ahead of the January 16, 2027 presidential election. It also urged media organisations that published the disputed report to review the full footage of the senator’s address and correct what it described as a misrepresentation. “Political disagreement is legitimate; misrepresentation is not,” the statement added. item.title: 2027: Any Igbo against Obi is enemy of Ndigbo – Victor Umeh
item.description: Senator Victor Umeh, representing Anambra Central Senatorial District, has declared that any Igbo person opposed to the presidential ambition of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) candidate, Peter Obi, is an enemy of Ndigbo. Umeh, who described Obi as the conscience of the Igbo people, also cautioned political leaders in the South-East, particularly the Anambra State Government, against working against the former governor’s presidential ambition ahead of the 2027 general elections. The senator, popularly known as Ohamadike, made the remarks in a trending video, on Monday. He said Obi represented the collective aspirations of the Igbo people and urged the people of the South-East to rally behind him. “I’m an Igbo activist, you people know me and you hear my voice in the Senate on all issues of national importance. Peter is our conscience in this election. Any Igbo man who stands up to say we will not vote for Peter Obi, I’m telling you that he’s an enemy of Igbo people,” Umeh said. He specifically warned the Anambra State Government against allegedly opposing Obi’s ambition for political reasons, arguing that the state’s leadership should consider the broader interests of the Igbo people. Umeh claimed he played a significant role in the emergence of Governor Chukwuma Soludo, insisting that the office of governor was held in trust for the collective interest of the people. “This government in the state, I helped installing it. Nobody came here the governor of Anambra State since 2003 without my input. This one that is serving, I was a principal contributor to his ascending to that office. He’s holding that office on trust for all of us,” he said. The senator urged Soludo not to undermine Obi’s presidential ambition, describing any attempt to work against his kinsman as an abomination. “Let him not commit what is called abomination by wanting to destroy his brother in the name of politics,” he warned. Umeh further argued that if politicians from other geopolitical zones were free to mobilise support for President Bola Tinubu, Igbo people should equally be allowed to rally behind Obi without intimidation or condemnation. Recalling Obi’s support for him, the senator called on Ndigbo to stand for what he described as truth and justice, adding that Obi’s success in the 2027 presidential election would be a collective achievement for the South-East. “He told me this is his time and if he makes it, the Igbos have made it. So let nobody come and insult us and our intelligence,” Umeh added. The post 2027: Any Igbo against Obi is enemy of Ndigbo – Victor Umeh appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: FG considers assessment tests for Nigerians with foreign degrees before NYSC
item.description: The Federal Government is considering the introduction of assessment test for Nigerians who obtain degrees from foreign institutions, particularly in African countries. Dr Folake Olatunji-David, Acting Permanent Secretary, Federal Ministry of Education, disclosed this at the 37th meeting of the National Standing Committee (NSC) on Evaluation of Foreign Qualifications in Abuja on Monday. Olatunji-David said the assessment test was necessary before their qualifications would be evaluated for mobilisation into the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC). She said the proposal was aimed at ensuring that foreign qualifications presented by Nigerians reflected genuine learning achievements and met the required academic standards. She explained that the measure was particularly important given the increasing number of Nigerians studying in foreign higher institutions, especially in West Africa. “We must ensure that the standard of education in Nigeria is not lowered by allowing all manner of foreign qualifications that are not recognised to be paraded by Nigerians without the corresponding learning achievement. “In as much as we want to encourage global socialisation, education, and the rest of them because the world is a global village now, but we want to maintain standard. “We want to ensure that, yes, for every certificate given, they are earned, and they can produce people that can contribute positively to our national development. “I therefore invite this committee once again to consider, if necessary, an assessment test before such graduates are evaluated for NYSC,” she said. Olatunji-David described the committee as central to efforts to safeguard the integrity of Nigeria’s education system by ensuring that only genuine and duly accredited foreign qualifications were recognised. She expressed concern over the rising cases of forgery of Nigerian and foreign degree certificates, saying the ministry was taking steps to address the menace. The acting permanent secretary commended members of the committee for decisions reached at their previous meeting, describing them as important steps towards improving the evaluation and accreditation of foreign qualifications. She said the ministry had recorded progress in confirming the accreditation status of foreign institutions, issuing clearance letters for NYSC mobilisation, authenticating certificates and issuing no-objection letters. According to her, the ministry also issues eligibility and proficiency letters to Nigerians travelling abroad for employment or further studies. “Since the beginning of this year, the evaluation of foreign certificates and authentication of Nigerian certificates have been automated and digitalised, making the process seamless. “The fees accruing are remitted into government accounts, thereby increasing the ministry’s revenue generation,” Olatunji-David said. item.title: Edo APC chieftain killed by son over alleged prophecy
item.description: By Ozioruva Aliu BENIN CITY – A chieftain of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Fugar, Etsako Central Local Government Area of Edo State, Julius Bello, has been allegedly killed by his son, Irobudo, following a prophecy that reportedly blamed him for the suspect’s misfortunes. Bello, popularly known as De Lord Ogata, was reportedly attacked with a sledgehammer by his son, who struck him on the head. The incident occurred on Sunday, shortly after the suspect reportedly returned from Lagos at the weekend. Witnesses said the suspect allegedly attacked his father after a prophet told him that Bello was responsible for his poor state in life. The deceased was the APC Ward Three Chairman in Fugar, Etsako Central Local Government Area. The Edo State Police Command confirmed the killing, with its spokesperson, Eno Ikoedem, saying the command had commenced an investigation. The suspect was still at large as of the time of filing this report. The post Edo APC chieftain killed by son over alleged prophecy appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: ICPC files amended charge against Adeyemi, adds four civil servants
item.description: The Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) has filed amended charges against Adeniyi Adeyemi, the purported director general of the non-existent Presidential Foreign Intervention Promotion Council (PFIPC). The prosecution counsel, Sylvanus Tahir, SAN, told the court that ICPC expanded the previous 22 counts to 36. Tahir said that the four suspects are Aminu Abdullahi, Ogaba Harry, Florence Omameh and Patricia Akhigbe and included in the new charge. The case was originally filed by the Nigerian police. Monday’s proceedings, which originally slated for hearing of Adeyemi’s bail application, was halted because of the charge amendment, requiring all defendants, including Adeyemi, to enter their pleas. However, the plea taking could not proceed because the fourth defendant, Omameh, was absent from court on health grounds. The rest of the defendants were in court. ”Her unavailability in court has constrained the prosecution from proceeding with the arraignment, this being a criminal charge,” Tahir said. He relied on Section 266 of the Administration of Criminal Justice Act (ACJA) for his application. Tahir argued that an accused person has to be present in court throughout the trial, “subject to the exception stated therein.” He, therefore, urged the court for a short adjournment to allow the fourth defendant time to recover and enter her plea. Adeyemi’s counsel, Ibrahim Angulu, SAN, did not object to the amended charge or adjournment. However, he reminded the court of Adeyemi’s prolonged detention. Meanwhile, Justice Yusuf Halilu adjourned until Nov. 18 for the arraignment of the suspects. He, however, ordered that Adeyemi should be taken back to Kuje Correctional Facility and the other defendants to return to the ICPC detention facility. (NAN) The post ICPC files amended charge against Adeyemi, adds four civil servants appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Youth Olympics: Nwankwo, Bright Win Historic Gold In Men’s, Women’s 100m
item.description: Nigeria made an impressive start to the athletics competition at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games on Sunday, winning gold in both the men’s and women’s 100m finals at the Complexe Iba Mar Diop. Rosemary Nwankwo opened the country’s gold-medal account in the women’s 100m, crossing the finish line in 11.16 seconds to claim victory and set a new personal best. Nigeria’s Rosemary Nwankwo, gold medalist (C), Arwa Ali of the United Arab Emirates (L), silver medalist, and Dana Salem of Qatar (R), bronze medalist, pose on the podium after the women’s 100-meter track and field final at the 2026 Dakar Youth Olympic Games, held at the Iba Mar Diop Complex (CID Stadium) in Dakar on November 8, 2026. (Photo by NICOLAS REMENE / AFP) She finished ahead of Arwa Ali of the United Arab Emirates, who clocked 11.41 seconds, also a personal best, while Dana Salem of Qatar settled for bronze in 11.48 seconds. The win made Nwankwo the third Nigerian woman to take Youth Olympic 100m gold, following Josephine Omaka at the inaugural Singapore 2010 Games and Rosemary Chukwuma at Buenos Aires 2018. Nigeria’s Rosemary Nwankwo, winner of the women’s 100-meter track and field final at the 2026 Dakar Youth Olympic Games, poses next to the board at the Iba Mar Diop Complex (CID Stadium) in Dakar on November 8, 2026. (Photo by NICOLAS REMENE / AFP) Nigeria’s celebrations continued minutes later as Gift Bright secured another gold medal in the men’s 100m, finishing in a personal-best time of 10.28 seconds. China’s Zhang Hangyu came second in 10.57 seconds, while Poland’s Szymon Dolega claimed bronze in 10.61 seconds. Speaking after her triumph, Nwankwo said she remained focused on her race despite the significance of the occasion. Nigeria’s Gift Bright, react after winning the men’s 100-meter semifinal at the 2026 Dakar Youth Olympic Games, held at the Iba Mar Diop Complex (CID Stadium) in Dakar on November 8, 2026. (Photo by NICOLAS REMENE / AFP) “There was no pressure on me. I run my race. I focused on me, and I did it,” she said. “I’ve prayed for this moment, and I did it.” For Bright, the victory was particularly significant after a thigh injury had troubled him in the two weeks leading up to the competition. China’s Hangyu Zhang (L), silver medalist; Nigeria’s Gift Bright (C), gold medalist; and Poland’s Szymon Dolega (R), bronze medalist, pose on the podium after the men’s 100-meter track and field final at the 2026 Dakar Youth Olympic Games, held at the Iba Mar Diop Complex (CID Stadium) in Dakar on November 8, 2026. (Photo by NICOLAS REMENE / AFP) He admitted that the injury had affected his confidence but said he was relieved to compete without pain in the final. “I want to tell you guys that at the next (Youth) Olympics, expect Nigeria to win it again. We are good sprinters,” he said. We know how to condition ourselves to stay where we are. It’s a very big thing for us.” The post Youth Olympics: Nwankwo, Bright Win Historic Gold In Men’s, Women’s 100m appeared first on

item.title: PIA: Reps demand accountability, measurable benefits for Nigerians
item.description: …Say five years after enactment, reforms must boost production, revenue, investment By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja The House of Representatives has called for greater accountability in the management of Nigeria’s petroleum resources, insisting that the Petroleum Industry Act (PIA) must deliver increased oil production, higher government revenue, improved energy security, job creation and tangible benefits for Nigerians. The House said five years after the enactment of the legislation, the Federal Government and relevant institutions must demonstrate the impact of the reforms on the country’s oil and gas industry and the wider economy. Speaker of the House, Tajudeen Abbas, stated this on Monday at the opening of a three-day retreat on Petroleum Industry Act Implementation: The PIA, Corporate Governance and Legislative Oversight, organised by the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPC Ltd) in collaboration with the Office of the Speaker in Abuja. Abbas, who was represented by the House Leader, Julius Ihonvbere, said the success of the PIA should not be measured merely by the establishment of new institutions or the restructuring of the national oil company, but by its ability to deliver value from Nigeria’s petroleum resources. He described the PIA as one of the country’s most consequential economic legislations, designed to establish a transparent, commercially viable, accountable and investment-friendly petroleum industry. “Five years down the line, the central question is how much of that promise we have translated into practice,” he said. The Speaker noted that the transformation of the Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation into NNPC Ltd, the establishment of regulatory institutions and the introduction of a framework for host community development were intended to address longstanding challenges in the petroleum sector. He, however, stressed that the passage of the legislation must be followed by effective implementation to achieve its objectives. “The passage of a reform law is not the same as the successful implementation of that reform,” Abbas said. He identified crude oil theft, pipeline vandalism, production constraints, infrastructure deficiencies, investment uncertainty and regulatory bottlenecks as major challenges requiring urgent attention. According to him, protecting petroleum infrastructure remains critical to safeguarding national revenue and strengthening the country’s economic and security interests. “We recognise that the protection of national petroleum assets is not merely an industry concern; it is an economic and national security imperative,” he said. Abbas also called for adequate crude oil supplies to domestic refineries without undermining the commercial viability of upstream operations, noting that Nigeria must strengthen its domestic refining capacity and improve energy security. item.title: 2027: Shettima assures South-East of project completion, seeks votes
item.description: …As Nwifuru pledges Ebonyi support for Tinubu By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki The All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign train on Monday arrived in Abakaliki, the Ebonyi State capital, to canvass support for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid ahead of the 2027 general elections. Vice-President Kashim Shettima, who represented Tinubu at the rally, assured the people of Ebonyi State and the South-East of the completion of ongoing federal projects if the President is re-elected. Shettima also said the Tinubu administration had strengthened security in the South-East, particularly Ebonyi State, creating a safer environment for residents. He urged the electorate to come out en masse to vote for Governor Francis Nwifuru and other APC candidates in the forthcoming elections. In his remarks, Governor Nwifuru pledged the support of Ebonyi voters for Tinubu’s re-election, assuring the President of massive votes from the state. He said the South-East had suffered infrastructure deficits under previous administrations but maintained that the Tinubu government had changed the situation through projects across the region and other parts of the country, many of which are being supervised by the Minister of Works, Senator David Umahi. The governor appealed to the Federal Government to connect the southern part of Ebonyi State to the national electricity grid to improve power supply and support industrial development. He also urged Tinubu to approve and ensure the completion of the proposed railway project linking Ebonyi to Aba in Abia State and Port Harcourt in Rivers State. Nwifuru highlighted some achievements of his administration in the last three and a half years, particularly in the health and education sectors. He said his government had provided medical equipment and revitalised primary and secondary healthcare facilities across the state’s 13 local government areas. The governor also disclosed that work had commenced on the Abakaliki cement factory project, expressing optimism that its completion would create employment opportunities for young people. On education, he said his administration had recruited teachers for primary and secondary schools, adding that 314 beneficiaries of state scholarships had graduated with master’s degrees from overseas universities and commenced doctoral programmes in the United Kingdom. Also speaking, Umahi said Ebonyi State remained an APC stronghold and urged residents to support Tinubu’s second-term ambition to enable the administration to complete ongoing infrastructure projects. The minister listed several federal projects in the state, including the Afikpo-Cross River Ndibe Bridge, the Abakaliki-Afikpo road dualisation and the proposed superhighway linking Ebonyi, Enugu, Kogi, Benue, Nasarawa and Abuja. item.title: Obi Alleges NFF Blocked Him From Greeting Victorious Flamingos
item.description: The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) presidential candidate Peter Obi has alleged that officials of the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) prevented him from greeting members of the national Under-17 women’s football team, the Flamingos, following their historic victory at the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup. Obi said he was allegedly informed that the officials had warned against allowing him to approach the players, allegedly threatening that they would lose their jobs if he did. The former Anambra State governor disclosed this in a statement posted on his official X handle on Monday, after the Flamingos returned to Nigeria following their 2-1 victory over Japan in Saturday’s final in Morocco. Obi said he arrived at the airport at about 7 a.m. on Monday to board a flight to Enugu when he sighted the victorious team preparing to leave the airport. Flamingos arriving in Nigeria. He said he subsequently asked his protocol officer, Jackie Wayas, to find out whether he could greet and welcome the players. “With genuine joy and enthusiasm, I asked my Protocol Officer, Jackie Wayas, to find out whether I could greet and welcome the team. I was informed that officials of the Nigerian Football Federation (NFF) had refused and had requested that I not approach them because, if I did, they would all lose their jobs,” he wrote. Obi described the incident as another example of what he called the growing culture of “toxic politics” in Nigeria, alleging that he had experienced similar treatment during a previous visit to a football event. He recounted that on March 25, 2025, he travelled to Uyo, Akwa Ibom State, for a World Cup qualifying match, where he said the governor received him at the VIP stand. According to him, after the match, other government officials were allowed to greet the players, but he was again prevented from doing so. “Following the match, other government officials went to greet the players, but I was again prevented from doing so. I was told by the officials that they would lose their jobs if I proceeded,” he said. The former governor expressed concern over what he described as the increasing politicisation of public engagements, arguing that political differences should not prevent Nigerians from celebrating national achievements. “It is deeply troubling to witness the extent of toxic politics into which our nation has descended since 2025. Each year appears to bring further deterioration. This reflects how deeply Nigeria has been affected. “The new Nigeria we aspire to build must have no room for hostility, intimidation, or discrimination, regardless of political affiliation. It must be a Nigeria in which unity, mutual respect, and our shared humanity take,” he said. item.title: Ogun govt clarifies video of corps members sleeping in hall
item.description: By Enitan Abdultawab The Ogun State Government has described a viral video showing prospective corps members sleeping in a hall at the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) Orientation Camp in Sagamu, following concerns over accommodation conditions at the facility. The state government said the situation occurred during the registration exercise, which extended into the night, adding that the allocation of hostels and screening of prospective corps members were the exclusive responsibilities of NYSC officials. Special Adviser on Media and Strategy to Governor Dapo Abiodun, Kayode Akinmade, in a Facebook post on Monday, explained that prospective corps members were required to undergo credential verification and screening before being assigned accommodation. He said those whose registration extended into the night were temporarily accommodated in the multipurpose hall, where mattresses were provided for them to rest while the exercise continued. He stated: “The video captured a temporary arrangement during the registration exercise, which continued into the night. “The prospective corps members must first undergo credential verification and screening by NYSC officials before being allocated hostels. Those whose registration extended into the night were temporarily accommodated in the multipurpose hall, with mattresses provided for them to rest while the exercise continued.” Akinmade noted that Ogun State received more than 4,300 prospective corps members in the current batch, compared with slightly over 2,000 in previous batches, putting additional pressure on available camp facilities. He stressed that although NYSC handles registration, screening and hostel allocation, the state government supports the scheme through interventions aimed at improving the welfare of corps members. According to him, the state government provided 500 mattresses for the current exercise, while the Akarigbo of Remo donated 100 mattresses, followed by an additional 200. Akinmade also recalled that Governor Abiodun recently approved a ₦50,000 welfare grant for each of the 3,050 corps members in the 2026 Batch C, Stream I, to support their transportation. He added that Ogun State had been adjudged the best in the country in NYSC administration, describing the recognition as a reflection of the government’s sustained commitment to the scheme. The government urged the public to distinguish between the operational responsibilities of NYSC and the supportive role of the state, assuring that the Abiodun administration would continue to provide an enabling environment for corps members serving in Ogun. item.title: Meet only 2 countries to have won both men’s, women’s U-17 World Cups
item.description: Nigeria and France have emerged as the only two countries to have won both the men’s and women’s FIFA Under-17 World Cups following the Flamingos’ historic triumph at the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco. Nigeria achieved the milestone after its U-17 women’s team defeated Japan 2-1 in Saturday’s final in Rabat, becoming the first African nation to win the women’s competition. The victory also ended Nigeria’s 18-year wait for a FIFA U-17 title, having last won the men’s competition in 2015. According to FIFA’s records, France were previously the only country to have won both versions of the tournament, having secured the men’s title in 2001 and the women’s trophy in 2012. Nigeria’s five men’s U-17 World Cup titles Nigeria’s success in the men’s competition dates back to 1985, when the Golden Eaglets defeated West Germany 2-0 in Beijing to win the inaugural edition of the tournament, then known as the FIFA U-16 World Championship. The team went on to win the competition four more times, in 1993, 2007, 2013 and 2015. Its five titles make Nigeria the most successful country in the history of the men’s U-17 World Cup. The 2013 triumph came after a 3-0 victory over Mexico in the final, while the 2015 team defeated Mali 2-0 in Chile to become the first country to win consecutive editions of the tournament. How France achieved the double France became the first country to win both versions of the competition. The French men’s team won the 2001 FIFA U-17 World Championship in Trinidad and Tobago after defeating Nigeria 3-0 in the final. Eleven years later, France’s women’s team lifted the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Azerbaijan in 2012. They defeated North Korea 7-6 on penalties after a 1-1 draw in the final to claim their maiden title. France therefore held the distinction of being the only country to have won both competitions until Nigeria’s latest achievement. Flamingos end Nigeria’s long wait Nigeria’s historic achievement was secured through a 2-1 victory over Japan in the 2026 final. Awawu Bashiru opened the scoring in the 39th minute before Oluebube Umejiaku doubled Nigeria’s advantage two minutes into the second half. Japan reduced the deficit through Fuki Ito in the 80th minute, but the Flamingos held on to secure the trophy. The victory completed a remarkable campaign for the Nigerian side, which recovered from a 2-1 opening defeat to Poland to win its next six matches. The team also defeated Brazil 3-1 in the semi-finals to book its place in the final against Japan. The triumph was significant beyond Nigeria, as it marked the first time an African country had won the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup. It also made the Flamingos the first Nigerian women’s national team to win a FIFA World Cup title. With the latest achievement, Nigeria joins France in the exclusive group of countries to have won both the men’s and women’s FIFA U-17 World Cups. item.title: Presidency tackles Obi over alleged prevention from greeting Flamingos
item.description: The Presidency has accused opposition politicians of attempting to politicise Nigeria’s national sports teams, following a claim by former Anambra State governor, Peter Obi, that he was prevented from greeting members of the victorious Flamingos at an airport. The Special Assistant to the President on Social Media, Dada Olusegun, made the position known in a post on X on Monday, describing attempts to politicise national sports teams and institutions as distasteful. Obi, the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, had alleged that officials of the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) stopped him from approaching the Under-17 women’s national team after their return from the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco. Reacting to the allegation, Olusegun said national athletes, including the Flamingos, represented the entire country rather than any political party or individual. He explained that protocols governing national teams were designed to protect young athletes from political exploitation, commercial distractions and unnecessary media attention while on official duties. “The constant attempt by the opposition to politicize our national sports teams and institutions is highly distasteful,” he wrote. “Our national athletes, including the Under-17 girls’ team, represent the entire Federal Republic of Nigeria, not any specific political party or individual ambition. Protocol guidelines around national teams are designed strictly to protect young athletes from political exploitation, commercial distractions, and unnecessary media circuses while on official duty.” Addressing Obi directly, the presidential aide urged him to reconsider what he described as his tendency to manipulate situations and rely on unverified accounts to create a narrative of victimisation. “Mr Peter Obi, I hope you will reflect on your manipulative way of life and stop weaponising unverified hearsay to build a victim narrative. Let our athletes focus on winning for Nigeria, free from political theatre,” he wrote. Obi had earlier said he arrived at the airport around 7am on Monday while preparing to travel to Enugu when he sighted the Flamingos, who had just returned from Morocco. He said he asked his protocol officer, Jackie Wayas, to find out whether he could welcome the players but was informed that NFF officials had objected to his approach. According to Obi, the officials reportedly warned that they would lose their jobs if they allowed him to greet the team. The former governor also recalled an earlier incident on March 25, 2025, when he travelled to Uyo, Akwa Ibom State, for a World Cup qualifying match and was allegedly prevented from greeting members of Nigeria’s national team after the game. Expressing concern over what he described as a growing culture of toxic politics, Obi said the country should prioritise unity and mutual respect regardless of political differences. The Flamingos returned to Abuja on Monday following their 2-1 victory over Japan

item.title: Why I rejected Tinubu’s ministerial offer — Tunde Bakare
item.description: The Leader of Citadel Global Community Church, Pastor Tunde Bakare, has explained why he declined an offer by President Bola Tinubu to serve as a minister in his administration, saying he considered himself too old for the responsibilities of the office. Bakare said he preferred to support the government from behind the scenes by offering advice and proposing solutions to national challenges. The cleric disclosed this on Sunday while speaking at an event organised by Envoy Nation in Leicester, United Kingdom. He said he had told Tinubu that although he was not interested in joining his cabinet, he remained willing to contribute to national development through constructive advice whenever necessary. Bakare clarified that his decision to stay outside the government should not be interpreted as opposition to the Tinubu administration, insisting that he had never belonged to the opposition. He described himself as a platform for constructive suggestions, saying he would speak out whenever he identified shortcomings in government policies or actions and offer possible solutions. The former presidential candidate also reaffirmed his membership of the All Progressives Congress (APC), dismissing suggestions that he could easily switch political allegiance. He said, “I told Tinubu I’m too old to be a minister, but I will help in the background in any way I think will help my country. I have never been part of the opposition. I am a propositional platform, if I see something wrong, I will suggest a solution. “I can’t change sides quickly by joining one party today and another tomorrow. I am a full member of APC, and I will vote when the time comes.” Bakare’s remarks underscore his preference for contributing to governance through private counsel and constructive criticism rather than holding a formal position in the Tinubu administration. item.title: UK lists categories of migrants who can secure permanent residence after 5 years
item.description: The UK government has outlined categories of foreign nationals who will remain eligible to obtain permanent residence after five years, despite plans to extend the standard settlement period for most migrants to 10 years. Under its revised Earned Settlement policy, announced by Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood on November 2, 2026, the government intends to replace the existing five-year standard route to Indefinite Leave to Remain (ILR) with a system that rewards migrants based on their earnings, professional contributions and immigration history. However, certain categories of migrants will retain access to the five-year settlement pathway. According to the Home Office, the exemptions are intended to recognise the contributions of higher-earning migrants, essential public service workers and people who have served the UK through specific immigration routes. Migrants who can qualify for permanent residence after five years The following groups have been identified under the revised settlement framework: 1. High-earning foreign workers Migrants earning more than £50,271 annually will be eligible to apply for permanent residence after five years, provided they meet the income requirement for at least three of the five years preceding their application. This category covers foreign professionals whose earnings meet the government’s specified threshold. 2. Doctors, nurses and teachers Foreign nationals working in qualifying healthcare and education occupations will retain the five-year settlement pathway. The government specifically identified doctors, nurses and teachers as examples of professionals whose contributions to essential public services justify a shorter route to permanent residence. 3. Eligible care workers Care workers who entered or switched into the social care route during the period between 2022 and 2025 will retain the opportunity to secure permanent residence after five years. However, they must have complied with their visa conditions and earned at least £25,000 annually while working in the social care sector. The government said the exemption recognises the contribution of care workers during the period when Britain’s social care sector faced significant staffing shortages following the COVID-19 pandemic. 4. Eligible family members of British citizens Certain partners, parents and children of British citizens will also retain access to the five-year settlement pathway. The exemption covers eligible family visa applicants, although the precise eligibility conditions will depend on the applicable immigration rules. 5. Refugees arriving through approved safe and legal routes Foreign nationals granted refugee status after arriving in the UK through government-approved safe and legal routes will be eligible to apply for permanent residence after five years. However, refugees who arrive through irregular routes will face significantly longer waiting periods under the new framework. The government has proposed a 20-year settlement perio

item.title: Offa bank robbery: Kwara govt drops 18 charges against Saraki, Ahmed
item.description: … add two new charges By Demola Akinyemi Ilorin In a dramatic twist, the Kwara State Government has filed an amendment to its initial 20-count charge against its two former governors, Dr Abubakar Bukola Saraki and Alhaji Abdulfatai Ahmed, over the 2018 Offa bank robbery case by dropping 18 of the original charges while retaining only two and adding two new charges. In the amended charge sheet with Charge Number KWS/114C/2026 signed by the State Attorney General, Senior Ibrahim Sulyman (SAN), sighted by journalists in Ilorin, the government by implication has now reduced the total number of charges to four. In the new charge sheet, Counts 1 and 2 accused Saraki, Ahmed, Yusuf Abdulwahab and Alabi Olalekan of “conspiring to belong to a gang of thieves” and “belonging to a gang of thieves”. Also, counts 3 and 4, accused the quartet of concealment and disappearance of a “vehicle used for illegal purpose”. A motion on notice for the amended charges dated November 6th, 2026, has been filed by the prosecution and supported by a 6-paragraph affidavit deposed to by Sulyman Mohammed-Jamiu, a litigation clerk in the office of the Kwara State AG. It will be recalled that at the last sitting of the State High Court on the case on November 5th, 2026, the judge, Justice Osuolale Ajayi, reserved his ruling on the issue of whether he could continue with the arraignment while the defendant has a pending application for a stay of proceedings on the matter at the Court of Appeal. The Court of Appeal on November 3rd, 2026, advised the lawyer, Abdulfatah Ahmed, J. A. Mumini, SAN, to formally make his application for the court to issue an order that the parties at the trial court should maintain status quo ante bellum instead of the oral submission that he made to the court. The appellate court then adjourned the case to November 12, 2026. The case at the trial court which commenced in April 2026 has not proceeded to trial as the court is still mired in several preliminary issues which have been taken to the appellate court. Contacted, a member of Saraki and Ahmed’s legal team described the struggle by the prosecution to press charges against the two former governors as “a mockery of the judicial process and an exercise in futility”. Vanguard reliably gathered that failure to make any headway by the Kwara state government may not be unconnected to the two pieces of legal advice issued in 2018 by the Office of the Federal Director of Public Prosecutions in the Office of the Attorney General of the Federation, who, after reviewing the police investigation file on the Offa robbery case in 2018, concluded that there is no evidence remotely or directly linking Saraki or Ahmed to the Offa robbery incident. item.title: UK issues guide for Nigerians, other nationals on accessing eVisa
item.description: The United Kingdom has released guidelines explaining how visa holders, including Nigerians, can access their electronic immigration status. UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI) published the instructions in an infographic shared on its official X account on Monday, outlining the process of setting up an account, confirming one’s identity and connecting it to an eVisa. An eVisa is an online record containing a person’s identity and immigration status. It shows the category of permission granted to an individual, including whether they have indefinite leave to remain in the UK, as well as the conditions attached to their immigration status. The UK government said electronic visas have replaced physical immigration documents, adding that individuals granted a UK visa or other permission to remain in the country would be issued an eVisa. How to apply for and access a UK eVisa 1. Submit a visa application Applicants must first complete the UK visa application process through the government’s official website, GOV.UK . Depending on the category of application, they may also need to provide biometric details and verify their identity at a designated Visa Application Centre. 2. Receive an application decision After submitting their applications, applicants will be notified by email once UK Visas and Immigration reaches a decision. The agency advises applicants to monitor their spam and junk folders to ensure they do not miss important notifications. 3. Set up a UKVI account Those whose applications are approved should proceed to create an account through the official eVisa portal at gov.uk/evisa. Applicants are required to follow the online instructions until the system confirms that their accounts have been successfully created. 4. Confirm identity and connect the eVisa After creating an account, users must log in and verify their identities using the UK Immigration: ID Check application. They are also required to link their UKVI accounts to their electronic immigration records to make the eVisas accessible online. 5. Access the electronic visa Once the eVisa is available, users will receive an email notification directing them to view their immigration status online. UKVI advises holders to review their digital records and ensure that all personal and immigration details are accurate before travelling. The UK government says creating a UKVI account and viewing an eVisa are free of charge. The post UK issues guide for Nigerians, other nationals on accessing eVisa appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 2027: INEC condemns ‘rig and die’ slogan, vows sanctions for electoral offenders
item.description: . Seeks media partnership to safeguard democracy . Warns against fake results, inflammatory rhetoric By Steve Oko & Chinedu Adonu The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has condemned the “rig and die” slogan being popularised by some political actors ahead of the 2027 general elections, warning that it could expose innocent Nigerians to electoral violence. The Commission also vowed that any electoral official, including ad hoc personnel, found to have compromised the electoral process would face the full weight of the law. INEC National Commissioner and Chairman, Information and Voter Education Committee, Mohammed Kudu Haruna, gave the warnings at a media engagement forum for journalists and media executives from the South-East, South-South and South-West geopolitical zones in Enugu. Haruna cautioned politicians against inflammatory rhetoric and threats capable of endangering ordinary Nigerians engaged as presiding officers, ad hoc staff, party agents and election observers. He stressed that disagreements over electoral outcomes should be resolved through lawful channels, including complaints to INEC, security agencies and the courts, rather than violence. The National Commissioner also sought stronger collaboration with the media to safeguard democracy and ensure credible, peaceful and transparent conduct of the 2027 elections. Describing the media as critical to electoral credibility, he said public confidence in the electoral process depended largely on the accuracy, fairness and professionalism of election reporting. He cautioned journalists against spreading misinformation, unverified results, manipulated videos and inflammatory political narratives capable of undermining public confidence and triggering violence. Haruna particularly warned against premature declaration of results, sensational reporting and presenting projections as official results. “Results are declared only by the Commission through its duly appointed returning officers. Projections and unofficial figures must be clearly labelled as such,” he said. He urged journalists to verify allegations against INEC through its official channels before publication and report electoral incidents with sensitivity, distinguishing between events personally witnessed and information obtained from other sources. The National Commissioner further called for inclusive election reporting that gives adequate attention to women, youths and persons with disabilities, particularly the challenges they face in participating in the electoral process. He urged media organisations to intensify voter education, especially on Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs), accreditation procedures, electronic transmission of results and peaceful participation. item.title: CHOGM 2026: Bianca seeks stronger commonwealth cooperation
item.description: Nigeria has called for stronger cooperation among Commonwealth member states to address security challenges, expand trade, strengthen democratic institutions and promote climate resilience. The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Bianca Odumegwu-Ojukwu, disclosed this on Monday in a post on her X account, detailing Nigeria’s expectations from the Commonwealth following her interventions at the 2026 Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM) in Antigua. She said Nigeria emphasised the need for collective action on peace and security, trade, climate resilience and youth empowerment, particularly in combating terrorism and expanding access to development finance. Odumegwu-Ojukwu also drew attention to Nigeria’s preparations for the 2027 general elections, stressing the importance of supporting free, fair and credible electoral processes through election monitoring groups and stronger democratic institutions across member states. According to her, Nigeria, under President Bola Tinubu’s leadership, remains committed to promoting democracy, consensus, civil, political and social rights, while upholding the rule of law and judicial independence. She described the creation of the Commonwealth Trade Portal as a welcome development, noting that trade facilitation initiatives would promote economic growth, strengthen trade links among member states and help developing economies integrate into the global financial market. The minister further urged the Commonwealth to give greater attention to women and girls affected by conflicts, displacement and climate change. She said their access to essential services, livelihood opportunities and justice should remain central to collective responses, adding that their voices must shape solutions to the challenges they face. On reparatory justice, Odumegwu-Ojukwu identified the agenda as a major highlight of the ministerial meeting, particularly the agreement by the United Kingdom government to engage in structured, time-bound, inclusive and good-faith dialogue with affected countries over the transatlantic trafficking of enslaved Africans and its historical consequences. She said Nigeria hoped that the commitments adopted at CHOGM 2026 would translate into practical actions capable of creating jobs, strengthening security and improving the lives of citizens across Commonwealth member states. item.title: PFIPC Scandal: FG Files Fresh Amended Charges Against Adeyemi Adeniyi, Four Others
item.description: The Federal Government has filed a fresh 36-count amended charge against the embattled Director-General of the Presidential Foreign Investment Promotion Council (PFIPC), Adeyemi Adeniyi, and four others over alleged forgery, false representation and fraud. Adeniyi appeared alongside his co-defendants before Justice Halilu Yusuf of the Federal Capital Territory High Court in Maitama, Abuja, on Monday. However, their arraignment on the fresh charges could not proceed due to the absence of the fourth defendant, Florence Omemah, who was reportedly ill. Prosecution counsel, Sylvanus Tahir, informed the court that Ms Omemah was receiving treatment at a hospital in Abuja. He subsequently requested a seven-day adjournment to enable her to recover and appear in court to take her plea. Counsel to Mr Adeniyi, Ibrahim Angulu, however, urged the court to grant a shorter adjournment to allow him to pursue bail for his client. He also told the court that Mr Adeniyi had been in detention for more than 200 days. In a brief ruling, Justice Yusuf adjourned the case until November 18 for the arraignment of all the defendants. The judge further ordered that Mr Adeniyi be remanded at the Kuje Correctional Centre, while the other defendants should remain in the custody of the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC). Alleged Fake Government Agency Adeniyi Adeyemi paraded himself as the DG of the PFIPC. Photo: X@BayoOnanuga. The case centres on allegations that Adeniyi established a fictitious federal agency known as the Presidential Foreign Investment Promotion Council and falsely presented himself as its director-general. Investigators alleged that the agency had no legal backing and that Mr Adeniyi forged appointment letters and signatures attributed to the Chief of Staff to the President to legitimise his purported position. According to investigators, he occupied offices previously used by the defunct Presidential Economic Advisory Council at the Federal Secretariat in Abuja and allegedly held unauthorised meetings with foreign diplomats. He was also accused of seeking official visa documentation for United States visas and operating 34 bank accounts. Investigators further alleged that he exploited loopholes in the civil service system to secure a proposed allocation of ₦1.302 billion for the fictitious agency in the 2026 budget. ICPC Uncovers Other Alleged Fake Agencies Following an interim report presented to President Bola Tinubu, the ICPC reportedly uncovered two other allegedly fictitious agencies linked to Mr Adeniyi: the FCT Investment Promotion Agency and the Foreign Investment Promotion Agency. The commission also recommended disciplinary action against some public officials suspected of assisting the alleged scheme. In October 2026, the Federal High Court in Abuja struck out the initial eight-count charge after jurisdictional concerns prompted the Attorney-General of the Federation to withdraw the case. item.title: Musiala’s condition cannot be cured, may never return to best — Bayern president
item.description: Bayern Munich honorary president Uli Hoeness has raised concerns over Jamal Musiala’s long-term future, saying the Germany international is suffering from a condition that cannot be permanently cured and may never regain his previous level of performance. According to BBC Sport, Hoeness said the 23-year-old forward’s condition could only be managed to some extent with medication, leaving the club uncertain about whether he would return to his best. “We are facing a dilemma in this case, as he is suffering from an illness that cannot simply be cured, but it can be controlled to a certain extent with the use of medication,” Hoeness told Bavarian broadcaster BR24. He also questioned whether Musiala would ever recover the level he displayed before his health problems, while acknowledging that Bayern would continue to support the player, who is under contract until 2030. “But the question remains: will he one day be able to regain the level he used to show?” Hoeness said. Hoeness further suggested that the situation had created a contractual dilemma for the German champions, claiming Musiala’s condition was not covered by the insurance attached to his deal. “Imagine if Bayern Munich now decided to question his contract, and told him: what you are able to offer currently no longer matches the level stipulated in the contract,” he said. Musiala’s health concerns emerged during pre-season after he collapsed twice within four days. He was subsequently reported to have a treatable neurological dysfunction. The forward has also been sidelined by a hamstring injury sustained in September and has yet to feature for Bayern since then, although he has recently returned to training. He has scored twice in four appearances for the German champions in all competitions this season. Former Bayern and Germany captain Lothar Matthaus, however, interpreted Hoeness’ comments as an attempt to challenge and motivate the youngster rather than write him off. “He’s needling him a little. It’s not just about wrapping him in cotton wool. He also has to battle against adversity sometimes,” Matthaus told Sky90. Matthaus added that Hoeness wanted Musiala to respond to the remarks by proving he could return to his previous level. “Uli was looking to create that adversity with this statement. “It’s fine for him to say something like that, because we can’t just put a positive spin on things and somehow wait for him to come back. “If I were in Jamal Musiala’s position, that would be motivation enough to show Uli I’m back.” Musiala joined Bayern in 2019 after coming through Chelsea’s academy and has since scored 71 goals and provided 38 assists in 235 appearances for the club. He has earned 46 caps for Germany and shared the Golden Boot as joint-top scorer at Euro 2024. item.title: DisCos Apologise To Nigerians Over Power Outages
item.description: Electricity Distribution Companies (DisCos) have apologised to Nigerians over persistent electricity shortages across the country, acknowledging the hardship caused by weeks of prolonged blackouts. Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of the Association of Nigerian Electricity Distributors (ANED), Sunday Oduntan, tendered the apology on Monday during an appearance on Channels Television’s Sunrise Daily . “I’d like to first of all start by apologising to Nigerians. Apology is needed; it is essential because Nigerians have been taken through this problem over the past few weeks,” he said. Oduntan also criticised what he described as a return to the blame game among operators in the electricity sector, recalling that similar disagreements between stakeholders had characterised the industry between 2016 and 2019. He said distribution companies, transmission operators, generation companies and gas suppliers had previously blamed one another for poor electricity supply instead of addressing the underlying problems. “Our major problem is that we have started that very wrong route that we went through between 2016 and 2019. What is that? Blame game. “Part of what happened at that time is that people will blame the DisCos, DisCos will blame TCN, TCN will blame GenCos, GenCos will blame the gas suppliers, and gas suppliers will blame payment issues. We have returned to that, and I think there is a need to arrest that,” he said. Oduntan Questions Conflicting Explanations A combo of the Chief Executive Officer of the Association of Nigerian Electricity Distributors (ANED), Sunday Oduntan and electricity installations. The ANED spokesperson also expressed concern over statements issued by the Nigerian Independent System Operator (NISO) and the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPC) regarding the factors responsible for the electricity shortages. He said NISO had attributed the supply challenges partly to low water levels and inadequate gas supply, while the NNPC subsequently issued a statement indicating that gas was available. Oduntan, however, questioned the information provided by the national oil company, insisting that it should clarify whether outstanding payments were affecting gas supply to power generation companies. “From the NNPC statement, it is very clear that they came to tell us half-truths. What I would have expected NNPC to do is to go ahead and talk to us whether there are payment issues. We need to know whether gas was paid for and delivered, who did, who didn’t,” he said. The ANED CEO urged the Minister of Power to intervene by bringing the relevant stakeholders together to establish the actual causes of the shortages. “This back and forth blame game between gas suppliers, NNPC and, of course, TCN or NISO, I think the Minister of Power needs to take charge.
